title: Waves & Sound
subject: Physics
tagline: A ripple on a pond, a guitar note, a sonic boom: energy travels while the matter stays put. Learn the wave equation, then see and hear it in harmonics, organ pipes, beats and the Doppler shift.

lessons.title: What Is a Wave?
lessons.summary: A wave carries energy without carrying the medium along. Transverse and longitudinal waves, compressions and rarefactions, and the one equation that links them all: v = fλ.

lessons.title: The Travelling-Wave Equation
lessons.summary: y = A sin(kx − ωt): which way the wave goes, how fast, and what each particle is doing. Phase differences, particle velocity versus wave velocity, and how to read a snapshot.

lessons.title: How Fast? The Speed of Waves
lessons.summary: √(T/μ) on a string and √(γP/ρ) in a gas, including Newton’s mistake and Laplace’s fix. The effects of temperature, pressure and humidity, a rope hanging under its own weight, and the energy a wave carries.

lessons.title: Superposition, Interference & Reflection
lessons.summary: Waves pass straight through each other and add along the way. Loud and quiet spots from two sources, the maximum and minimum intensity ratio, and what happens to a pulse at a fixed end, a free end or a joint.

lessons.title: Standing Waves on Strings
lessons.summary: Two waves travelling in opposite directions make one that stays put: nodes, antinodes and harmonics. The sonometer’s laws, consecutive resonances, and a string driven until it sings.

lessons.title: Organ Pipes & the Resonance Tube
lessons.summary: Air columns open at both ends or closed at one, which harmonics each allows, end correction, and the resonance-tube experiment for measuring the speed of sound, which you carry out yourself in the lab.

lessons.title: Beats
lessons.summary: Two nearly equal notes throb at the difference of their frequencies. Hear it, see the envelope, tune a mystery fork by ear, and learn the wax-and-file rules JEE loves.

lessons.title: The Doppler Effect
lessons.summary: Why a passing siren drops in pitch: moving sources, moving observers, wind, motion at an angle, echoes from moving reflectors, and the Mach cone of a sonic boom.

lessons.title: Wrap-up: The Waves Toolkit
lessons.summary: Strings and pipes side by side, the traps examiners like, a game called Wave Rush and a final mix of previous-year questions.
